chunks: 3387 - And in the Nawadir of Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from more than one of our companions, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام:

Concerning a man who collected the dowry of his daughter from her husband and then died: does she have the right to demand her dowry from her husband, or is her father's receipt considered her own receipt?

So he عليه السلام said: "If she had authorized him to collect her dowry from her husband, then she has no right to demand it. But if she had not authorized him, then she has that right, and the husband may seek recovery of that from her father's heirs, unless she was at that time a minor under his care; then it is permissible for her father to collect her dowry on her behalf. And whenever he divorces her before consummation, then her father may waive part of the dowry and take part of it, but he has no right to leave all of it. And that is the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic:"
“Except that they forgo, or the one in whose hand is the marriage tie forgives.”
Meaning the father, and the one whom the woman authorizes and entrusts with her affair, whether a brother, a relative, or someone else."

key_terms.صَدَاقِهَا: her dowry due from the husband
key_terms.عُقْدَةُ النِّكَاحِ: the bond or authority connected to the marriage contract
key_terms.وَرَثَةِ: the heirs from whom repayment may be sought
key_terms.وَكَّلَتْهُ: she appointed him as her agent

ai.seo_question: Can a woman reclaim her dowry if her father collected it from her husband?
ai.summary: This hadith explains legal rulings concerning agency in receiving a woman's dowry and clarifies when a father's receipt is legally valid on her behalf. It also connects the ruling about waiving part of the dowry before consummation to the Qur'anic phrase regarding the one who holds the marriage tie, identifying this as the father or an authorized representative.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3387 - In the book "Nawadir" by Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from multiple narrators among our companions, from Abu Abdullah (as):
Concerning a man who collected the dowry of his daughter from her husband and then passed away-can she demand her dowry from her husband, or is her father's collection considered her own collection?

Imam (as) said: "If she had authorized him to collect her dowry from her husband, then she has no right to demand it again. However, if she had not authorized him, then she has the right to claim it. In this case, the husband may seek repayment from the father's heirs-unless she was a minor under his care. In such a situation, the father's collection is valid on her behalf.
If the husband divorces her before consummation, the father may waive part of the dowry and retain part, but he does not have the authority to forgo the entire amount. This is based on the verse of Allah (swt), the Exalted:
'Except when they waive it or he (the guardian) in whose hand is the marriage contract waives it.' (Surah Al-Baqarah 2: 237)
This refers to the father or anyone the woman appoints and entrusts with her affairs, such as a brother, a relative, or others."
